name: Design the Strategic Portfolio and annual target exposures
summary: Once a year the Portfolio Design group in Total Fund Management turns the Board's Reference Portfolios and risk appetite into Strategic Portfolios, the intended mix of six asset classes and three regions five years out, and into target exposures and ranges for the coming fiscal year. Staff refresh long-term return and risk assumptions, map about 20 investment programs to return-risk factors, collect opportunity sets from the investment departments, build and stress-test candidate portfolios, and get an independent view from Risk. Department heads negotiate their program ranges, the Portfolio Strategy Committee and the ISRC endorse the result, and the Board approves it with the business plan. The cycle takes months because departments with competing ambitions need several rounds, assumptions are contested and each committee meets on its own calendar.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager with C$539 billion of net assets that sets one total portfolio for the base and additional plan and invests mostly through internal teams.
baseline.notes: Fiscal year runs April to March; the cycle is assumed to start in the autumn and finish before April 1.

trigger: The annual planning calendar opens the cycle, using the Board-approved Reference Portfolios and risk appetite and ISRC guidance.
end_state: The Board-approved Strategic Portfolios and current-year target exposures are loaded into the risk and data platforms and published to departments, capital allocation, financial planning and Risk.

volume.seasonality: One cycle a year, concentrated from autumn to the February and March Board meetings; a fuller review of the strategic mix at least every three years.

evidence.note: TFM's annual portfolio design process (F2021); strategic mix reviewed at least triennially (F2022).

roles.title: Senior Managing Director and Chief Investment Officer

evidence.note: The CIO is accountable for designing the Strategic Portfolios and chairs the Portfolio Strategy Committee (F2022). FTE from hands-on time over the annual cycle.
A TFM group head leads the negotiation with departments. FTE is the author's estimate from about 60 hours a year.
A Portfolio Design director runs the annual cycle. FTE is the author's estimate.
Portfolio Design principals own the scenario, liquidity and target work. FTE is the author's estimate.
Senior associates refresh assumptions, run optimisations and draft papers. FTE is the author's estimate.
Associates gather exposures and department submissions and load targets. FTE is the author's estimate.
TFM designs the portfolio in conjunction with the Risk group (F2021). FTE is the author's estimate.

roles.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
roles.department: Office of the President and CEO

evidence.note: The CEO chairs the ISRC, which oversees portfolio design. FTE from about 2 hours a year.

systems.name: Risk analytics platform (potential loss, limits, stress tests)
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse
Document management and investment committee memo repository

steps.name: Launch the annual design cycle
steps.description: A Portfolio Design director sets the timetable against the business planning calendar and Board dates, confirms whether this year is a full triennial review of the strategic mix or an annual confirmation, and collects the Board-approved Reference Portfolios, risk appetite and any ISRC guidance.

error.defect_description: The timetable leaves too little time before the Board meeting for a second round with departments.

control.basis: ISC terms of reference 5.1: annual review of the Investment Framework and review of Strategic Portfolios at least every three years

evidence.note: Annual framework review and at least triennial review of the strategic mix. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Refresh long-term return and risk assumptions
steps.description: A senior associate updates long-horizon expected returns, volatilities and correlations for the key return-risk factors, using the Chief Investment Strategist's research notes, climate scenarios and market data, and documents every change from last year.

error.defect_description: A stale correlation or inconsistent currency basis in the assumption set.

evidence.note: Long-run return views include estimated climate impacts; optimisation inputs drive the result. Effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Challenge assumptions with research and Risk
steps.description: A principal runs a review session with the investment strategy researchers and Risk, walks through each changed assumption and its effect on candidate portfolios, and records the agreed set.

error.defect_description: A disputed assumption is carried forward without a recorded decision.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; weights are highly sensitive to small input changes, so assumptions are commonly challenged before use.

steps.name: Update program exposures and factor mappings
steps.description: An associate pulls current exposures for each of about 20 investment programs from the risk platform and data platform, maps each program to the return-risk factors, regions and asset classes, and fills gaps for private holdings with proxies.

error.defect_description: A private program is mapped with a stale or wrong proxy, misstating its factor exposure.

evidence.note: Programs are modelled by their factor exposures; illiquid assets lack good proxies. Effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request opportunity sets from departments
steps.description: The associate sends each investment department's business management team a template for its one-year and five-year opportunity set, expected deployment, capacity and return expectations by program, with a due date.

error.defect_description: A template asks for figures on a different basis from last year.

evidence.note: TFM works with departments on opportunity areas over one- and five-year periods. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Consolidate department submissions
steps.description: As submissions arrive from Active Equities, Credit Investments, Private Equity, Real Assets and Capital Markets and Factor Investing, the associate chases late ones, puts them on one basis and flags figures that conflict with history or capacity.

error.defect_description: Optimistic deployment figures are taken at face value.

evidence.note: Departments and Risk give input on the range of attractive investment areas. The 2 to 4 week response time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Build candidate strategic portfolios
steps.description: A senior associate runs the optimisation and simulation models to build candidate portfolios at the targeted risk level for the base and additional plan, applying constraints for department capacity, geography, liquidity and leverage, and summarises weights by asset class and region five years out.

error.defect_description: A constraint is set wrongly or an input error produces a concentrated, unrealistic mix.

evidence.note: Strategic Portfolios are diversified at Reference Portfolio risk across six asset classes and three regions. Effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Rebuild candidates with revised constraints
steps.description: When departments, Risk or the committee reject the candidates, the senior associate changes the disputed constraints or assumptions, reruns the models and updates the weight tables, reusing most of the earlier set-up.

error.defect_description: A revised constraint is applied to one plan account but not the other.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; a rebuild reuses the model set-up, so it takes a fraction of the first build.

steps.name: Test liquidity, leverage and stress resilience
steps.description: A principal checks each candidate against the liquidity coverage and leverage limits, private asset funding needs and historical and hypothetical stress scenarios, and rejects or adjusts candidates that fail.

error.defect_description: A stress scenario misses a funding source that dries up in a crisis.

evidence.note: Leverage and liquidity limits apply to each Investment Portfolio; diversification is meant to improve resilience to downturns. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Risk reviews the candidates independently
steps.description: A Risk director reviews the candidates against the risk appetite, potential loss and concentration measures, checks the factor mappings and stress results, and writes a short independent view for the committee.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Risk Policy and integrated risk framework: independent risk input to portfolio design

next.condition: Risk asks for changes to candidates

evidence.note: TFM runs portfolio design with the Risk group, and the IRC oversees risk limit design. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Select the proposed portfolio
steps.description: The Portfolio Design director compares the candidates, the Risk note and the department submissions and picks a proposed Strategic Portfolio and the program deployment ranges to discuss with departments.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the director's role in narrowing the candidates.

steps.name: Negotiate program ranges with department heads
steps.description: A TFM managing director holds sessions with each department head on the proposed five-year deployment ranges, hears objections about capacity and opportunity, and agrees changes or escalates disagreements to the CIO.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: TFM narrows each program to its preferred five-year deployment range with departments; competition for capital across teams. Rework share and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Draft the Portfolio Strategy Committee paper
steps.description: A senior associate writes the committee paper with the proposed weights by asset class and region, the change from last year, expected return and risk, liquidity and leverage effects, Risk's view and the open issues.

error.defect_description: A table in the paper does not match the final model run.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of drafting effort for a committee paper.

steps.name: Managing director reviews the paper
steps.description: The TFM managing director reviews the paper for clarity and consistency with what was agreed with departments and returns it with comments if needed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Portfolio Strategy Committee reviews the proposal
steps.description: The Chief Investment Officer chairs the Portfolio Strategy Committee, which discusses the proposal with department and Risk representatives, gives guidance on key design targets and either endorses it or asks for alternatives.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISRC sub-committee mandate: PSC chaired by the CIO gives guidance on key portfolio design targets

evidence.note: PSC, chaired by the CIO, guides key portfolio design targets. Meeting wait and rework share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: ISRC endorses the Strategic Portfolio
steps.description: The CEO chairs the Investment Strategy and Risk Committee, which reviews the endorsed proposal together with the business plan and risk appetite and endorses it for the Board or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISRC mandate: oversight of the strategy, design, management and governance of the Investment Portfolios

evidence.note: The ISRC, chaired by the CEO, oversees portfolio design. Wait and rework share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Prepare Board materials and the business plan section
steps.description: A senior associate turns the endorsed proposal into the Strategic Portfolio section of the business plan and the Board committee presentation, with the weight tables and the explanation of changes.

error.defect_description: A weight in the business plan table differs from the endorsed proposal.

evidence.note: The Business Plan includes confirmation or adjustment of the Strategic Portfolios. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: CIO signs off the Board materials
steps.description: The CIO reads the Board paper and business plan section, makes final edits and approves them for the board secretariat.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: CIO accountability for recommending the Strategic Portfolios and market risk and leverage targets

evidence.note: The CIO is accountable for designing and recommending the Strategic Portfolios. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Board approves the Strategic Portfolio
steps.description: The Board of Directors, an outside party, reviews the Strategic Portfolios as part of the annual business plan at its scheduled meeting and approves them or asks for more analysis.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Board authorities: Board approval of the annual business plan, which includes the Strategic Portfolios

evidence.note: Board approval is required for the annual business plan, which includes the Strategic Portfolios. Wait to the meeting date is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set current-year target exposures and ranges
steps.description: A principal translates the approved Strategic Portfolio into target exposures and allowed ranges for the coming fiscal year by asset class, region and pool for the base and additional plan, consistent with the expected deployment path.

error.defect_description: A range or pool weight is inconsistent with the approved five-year path.

evidence.note: TFM develops the current-year target exposures and range expectations; the business plan sets Target Portfolio allocation bands. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Risk aligns limits and monitoring
steps.description: The Risk director checks the new targets and ranges against the Board limits approved with the risk appetite and confirms what the daily limit monitoring will measure against from the start of the fiscal year.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Risk Policy: Board-approved market, liquidity and leverage limits reviewed annually

evidence.note: The Board reviews and approves risk, liquidity and leverage limits annually. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Load targets into the risk and data platforms
steps.description: An associate enters the new target weights and ranges into the risk platform and the enterprise data platform used by balancing and capital allocation, and a second person checks the loaded values against the approved table.

error.defect_description: A weight is keyed into the wrong pool or region.

control.basis: Four-eyes check of reference data changes

evidence.note: Author's estimate of how approved targets reach daily systems.

steps.name: Publish the Strategic Portfolio and targets
steps.description: The Portfolio Design director sends the approved Strategic Portfolio and current-year targets to department heads, the capital allocation team, financial planning and Risk, and files the cycle record.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: TFM aligns the investment activities of other departments with the portfolio design. Times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Departments reject the proposed ranges
exceptions.description: A department head disputes the capacity or opportunity assumptions behind its range, and the candidates are rebuilt with revised constraints before the committee paper.

exceptions.name: Committee asks for alternatives
exceptions.description: The Portfolio Strategy Committee asks to see portfolios with different leverage, regional or private asset weights, adding a full modelling round.

exceptions.name: Triennial review of the strategic mix
exceptions.description: In the year after a Reference Portfolio review, the factor mix and leverage are reconsidered from first principles, so the assumption and modelling steps take at the high end of their ranges.

exceptions.name: Risk asks for changes
exceptions.description: Risk finds a concentration or stress result outside appetite and asks for the candidates to be rebuilt.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from launch to publication of targets
benchmarks.population: Annual strategic portfolio design at a large Canadian pension investment manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate: an annual process that starts in the autumn and must finish before the fiscal year begins on April 1 (about six months), with department rounds and committee and Board dates in between.

benchmarks.unit: share of total, five years out

evidence.note: Figures do not add due to rounding.

pain_points.description: Departments negotiate for capital, so ranges go through several rounds and modelling is repeated.

evidence.note: Five-year deployment ranges are narrowed with each department; competition for capital.

pain_points.description: Optimised weights swing with small changes in long-term assumptions, so assumptions are contested and rerun.

evidence.note: Weights are highly sensitive to small input changes.

pain_points.description: Private holdings have no clean market proxy, so factor exposures and stress results rest on judgement.

evidence.note: Illiquid assets may lack a satisfactory proxy; programs are mapped to factors.

pain_points.description: Waiting for committee and Board dates takes more time than the analysis.

evidence.note: Author's reading of the committee chain.

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)
sources.supports: Strategic Portfolios: six asset classes and three regions, indicative allocations five years out (base plan public equity 23%, private equity 23%, public fixed income 32%, credit 17%, real assets 31%, cash and absolute return -27%); strategic mix of factor exposures and leverage reviewed at least triennially; CIO accountable for designing Strategic Portfolios and recommending market risk and leverage targets; ISRC with Portfolio Execution, Portfolio Strategy, Investment Risk and Operational and Legal Risk committees; Business Plan includes the Strategic Portfolios; leverage defined (term debt, commercial paper, secured borrowing, synthetic financing); recourse leverage C$122 billion in F2022, 18% to 25% of net assets over five years; Board limit of 45% of net assets from April 1, 2022, reviewed yearly with risk appetite; 10-day liquidity coverage ratio 2.9x against 1.0x; leverage-related expenses C$295 million. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

Later than the reference period; used for practice. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: From Vision to Execution: How investors are operationalizing the total portfolio approach
sources.publisher: Thinking Ahead Institute, WTW and CAIA Association
sources.supports: Total portfolio approach practice: at the model fund a central investment committee coordinates capital allocation across asset classes and a central portfolio construction group brings exposures together; competition for capital based on marginal contribution to the total portfolio; reference portfolios as the board's risk anchor. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Principles of Asset Allocation (refresher reading)
sources.supports: Asset allocation steps: mean-variance optimisation with constraints, reverse optimisation and Black-Litterman views, high sensitivity of weights to small input changes, Monte Carlo and scenario tests, proxies for illiquid assets, risk budgeting, liability-relative approaches and rebalancing ranges.

assumptions: The ISRC step uses the CEO role, who chairs it; the process map lists only TFM roles and a Risk director, so other ISRC members' time is not counted.
Department heads' and their business management teams' time on submissions and negotiation is not counted here; it shows as waits at s06 and s11.
The Board's approval is taken to come through the annual business plan at a February or March meeting; the Board committee that reviews it first is not modelled separately.
Trigger shares are the author's split: the annual Board-approved risk appetite starts most cycles, with the Reference Portfolio decision mattering in triennial review years.
Hands-on hours are the author's estimates; the 20-person Portfolio Design group also runs the Reference Portfolio review, research and ad hoc analysis, which are outside this process.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file.
